clue.text: Plant with strange aroma is full of power

indicators.note: is full of says the rearranged letters hold another piece inside them
strange signals that the letters of aroma and is are put into an odd new order

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A gardener notices a plant whose peculiar scent is overpoweringly strong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' gives MARIOSA and 'is full of' takes in the P; the flower's name is Spanish for butterfly, after its delicate petals.
explanation.definitionFit: The mariposa lily is a North American flowering plant of the genus Calochortus.

clue.text: Ordered famous airman to finish prematurely

indicators.note: finishing prematurely means the word stops short, losing its final letter

parts.note: Douglas Bader was a celebrated RAF fighter pilot of the Second World War who flew with artificial legs

explanation.surface: A commander orders a celebrated pilot to cut his mission short.
explanation.walkthrough: Douglas Bader was a famous British wartime fighter pilot; 'to finish prematurely' cuts his name before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of bid, in the sense of commanded or instructed someone to do something.

clue.text: Line worker put around church window

indicators.note: put around says one piece is wrapped about the other, enclosing it

parts.note: an ant is the crossword's stock worker, from the worker ants of a colony
CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: A labourer on the job fits a frame around a church window.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put around' makes ANCET; 'church window' reads as one phrase, but church is wordplay and only 'window' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A lancet is a tall narrow pointed-arched window typical of Early English Gothic churches.

clue.text: Fruit around Australia gets praise

indicators.note: around says the fruit encloses the other piece inside it

parts.note: an apple is a fruit

explanation.surface: Australian fruit growers are celebrated for their produce.
explanation.definitionFit: Clapping is public praise or approval, so the two nouns are near synonyms.

clue.text: Asleep, Carol is interrupted by awful rumble

indicators.note: being interrupted means something breaks into the middle of the word

parts.note: to carol is to sing joyfully

indicators.note: awful suggests the letters of rumble are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Carol-singing is drowned out by a terrible rumbling noise while someone sleeps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' makes LUMBER and 'is interrupted by' sets it in the middle; 'Carol' looks like a woman's name but is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To slumber is to sleep, so the participle describes someone in a state of sleep.

clue.text: Plant eaten up, releasing energy somehow

indicators.note: somehow says the remaining letters are arranged in some other way
releasing means letting one letter go from the words

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A plant has been eaten up, and its energy is somehow given off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'releasing' drops one E from EATENUP, leaving ATENUP, which 'somehow' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The groundnut is a leguminous plant whose pods ripen underground, as well as the nut itself.

clue.text: A vehicle's following another — and some others

indicators.note: following says the second part comes after the first in the answer

parts.note: another vehicle, after the first one named, is a car
a van is a vehicle; with the 's it gives vans

explanation.surface: A queue of traffic: one vehicle behind another, and several more besides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some others' continues 'A vehicle ... another': caravans are further vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Caravans are towed trailers used as mobile homes, here simply more vehicles on the road.

clue.text: Representative and politician engaged in commercial activity

indicators.note: engaged in says the politician is set inside the other word

parts.note: a sale is a commercial transaction
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A sales rep and a Member of Parliament both get involved in business dealings.
explanation.definitionFit: A typical selection taken to stand for the whole, as in a representative specimen.

clue.text: Instrument for shaping clay bed

definitions.meaning: a flat wooden blade potters use to mould and smooth their work
a straw mattress or makeshift sleeping place on the floor

explanation.definitionFit: Pallet names both a potter's shaping paddle and a hard, simple straw bed.

clue.text: Discharge energy

definitions.meaning: to shoot a gun, or to dismiss an employee
passion or ardour, as in someone full of spirit

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to shoot or sack; the noun means fervour or spirit.

clue.text: Remark about exercise involving fifty members of crew

indicators.note: about says the remark surrounds the inner pieces

parts.note: a comment is a remark

indicators.note: involving says the exercise letters take in the numeral

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Someone comments on a training session that included fifty sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' gives PLE and 'about' wraps it; do not confuse with compliment, the remark of praise the surface hints at.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's complement is its full crew, the number of people needed to man it.

clue.text: Favouring dull layout

parts.note: to be for something is to favour it
mat, or matt, describes a dull, non-glossy finish

explanation.surface: Someone prefers a plain, unexciting design for a page.
explanation.definitionFit: The arrangement or design of a document or publication is its general structure or presentation.

clue.text: Ex-PM following two others in musical interval

parts.note: John Major was British Prime Minister from 1990 to 1997
something coming after two others is in third place

explanation.surface: A former Prime Minister comes after two predecessors during a break in a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: John Major was a British Prime Minister; 'following two others' is a cryptic way of saying third.
explanation.definitionFit: An interval spanning four semitones, as from C up to E, in music theory.

clue.text: Honoured person deceased, having swallowed chemical compound

indicators.note: having swallowed means the first word takes the second inside it

parts.note: the late person is one who has died
urea is an organic chemical compound found in urine

explanation.surface: An award winner who has died turns out to have ingested a chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: A laureate is someone honoured for achievement, like a Nobel prizewinner or poet.

clue.text: A thing without love, miserable

indicators.note: without says a letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: an object is a thing
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Someone without love feels like a mere wretched thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes the O (love, a zero score in tennis) from OBJECT.
explanation.definitionFit: Abject describes wretched, hopeless circumstances, as in abject poverty.

clue.text: Poorer society under Conservative folk who shouldn't sweep things under the carpet!

definitions.text: folk who shouldn't sweep things under the carpet!

indicators.note: under in a down clue puts the following pieces below the first one

parts.note: leaner means thinner or poorer, as in leaner times

explanation.surface: A political jibe: Tory rule leaves society poorer while hiding problems away.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: sweeping dirt under the carpet is the cardinal sin of people who tidy for a living.
explanation.definitionFit: Domestic staff who tidy houses ought to remove dust properly, not hide it under a rug.

clue.text: Something precious in one group of stars

parts.note: a gem is a precious stone
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A precious jewel sits inside a cluster of stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemini, the Twins, is a zodiac constellation.

clue.text: Greek character and I can turn up after one in institute

indicators.note: after says the reversed run follows the numeral in the answer

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: in a down clue, turn up means the pieces read from bottom to top

parts.note: eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A Greek student and a can are found at a college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up' reverses ETAITIN to NITIATE, and 'after' places it after I; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To institute something is to begin or set it up, a synonym of start.

clue.text: Heartless son longing to be a telltale

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the word is removed, leaving its ends

parts.note: an itch is a restless longing

explanation.surface: An unfeeling son who yearns to inform on others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' strips the O from SON, leaving SN.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean an informer who tells tales on others to authority.

clue.text: Good person to encourage Scottish politician

parts.note: ST abbreviates saint, a good person
to urge on is to encourage

explanation.surface: A saintly figure cheers on a politician from Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicola Sturgeon led the Scottish National Party and was First Minister of Scotland.

clue.text: London banker

parts.note: a banker here is something that has banks, a river, rather than a City financier

explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' suggests a City financier, but it means something with banks: a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The river flowing through the British capital has banks on both sides.

clue.text: Bird publication with bits half missing

parts.note: mag is short for magazine, a publication

indicators.note: half missing means the word loses half its letters

parts.note: pieces are bits

explanation.surface: A bird-watching magazine has some of its pages lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half missing' cuts PIECES to its first three letters, PIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A black-and-white corvid known for collecting shiny objects.

clue.text: Covering of long hair hiding end bits of tail

indicators.note: hiding says the hair conceals the other letters within it

parts.note: a mane is long hair, as on a horse or lion

indicators.note: end bits are the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A horse's flowing hair hides the tip of its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end bits of' takes T and L from TAIL, and 'hiding' puts them inside MANE.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantle is a cloak, or anything that covers or envelops, as in a mantle of snow.

clue.text: President in the bathroom? Not to be disturbed

parts.note: washing is what one might be doing in the bathroom, hence the query

indicators.note: to be disturbed means the letters of the word are shaken up

explanation.surface: A head of state in the bathroom hangs a do-not-disturb sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be disturbed' rearranges NOT into TON.
explanation.definitionFit: George Washington was the first President of the United States.

clue.text: Rugby home a wreck

parts.note: RU is Rugby Union
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A rugby club's home ground is a shambles.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean to destroy or spoil something completely, or a destroyed thing.

clue.text: It's odd having parking behind

parts.note: rum is old British slang for odd or strange
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: It is strange to park at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' looks like a direction for placing P, but it is the definition, a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Both nouns mean the buttocks or backside.

clue.text: More beloved member embraced by the German

indicators.note: embraced by says the member is held within the other word

parts.note: der is a German word for the
an ear is a member, or organ, of the body

explanation.surface: A beloved club member is hugged by a German.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of dear, meaning held in greater affection.

clue.text: The fellow overdue comes round in the afternoon to be companion

parts.note: he is a fellow, a man

indicators.note: comes round says the overdue word surrounds the time abbreviation

parts.note: late means overdue
PM, post meridiem, marks afternoon times

explanation.surface: A man who turns up late one afternoon to keep someone company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes round' builds LPMATE; the word also names a chess checkmate in which the defender helps, but here it is a partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A helpmate is a helpful partner, often a spouse, who provides companionship.
